maria.k: Drafting a concise runbook for new region cluster bring-up with GPU node pools (kubeadm/EKS/GKE/AKS notes). Sharing v1 here — please review, call out gaps (networking/quota/cost handoff).

maria.k: Summary checklist (high level):
1) Pre-checks: quotas, org/project perms, VPC subnets, peering, bastion access.
2) Infra provisioning: terraform for infra (VPC, subnets, NAT, LB), reserve static IPs, cloud DNS entries.
3) Cluster bootstrap: EKS/GKE/AKS or kubeadm variant, set up control plane & node pools with GPU SKUs.
4) Base addons: CNI, metrics, logging, storage class, GPU device plugin, nvidia drivers (if not provided), kube-proxy mode.
5) Validation: node readiness, GPU scheduling, sample inference job, perf smoke test (p95 latency), cost SLO smoke.
6) Handoff: runbook link, oncall rotate, billing alert thresholds, quota increase tickets.

maria.k: EKS-specific quick commands (example):
```bash
# create node group with GPUs (p4d/p3/rtx) via eksctl + TF:
eksctl create nodegroup --cluster my-cluster --name gpu-pool --node-type p4d.24xlarge --nodes 2 --nodes-min 2 --nodes-max 4 --node-labels role=gpu,instance=gpu
```
Notes: prefer managed nodegroups for lifecycle, but use self-managed for custom AMIs with proprietary drivers.

maria.k: kubeadm/airgap note: if customer wants private deployment, follow airgapped doc: pre-seed container registry, bake nodes with NVIDIA drivers, ensure NTP/time sync, disable cloud metadata accessor if required.

jon.s: Add a preflight step to verify region GPU SKUs & limits. Cloud consoles often show misleading availability. I usually run this: `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zones=us-west1-a` and `aws ec2 describe-instance-type-offerings --filters Name=location,Values=us-west-2` to confirm. Also add a ticket template to request quota increases early.

kevin.l: +1 on quota ticket. Also: include cost-control defaults for new node pools: autoscaling limits, node drainage policy, max-spot-percentage. Recommend default to mixed spot+on-demand with `maxSurge` small for nodes that serve critical RL workloads. Example TF snippet we use (short):
```hcl
node_pool {
  instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge", "p4d.8xlarge"]
  scaling = { min = 0, max = 8 }
  spot_percentage = 60
}
```
We should require an approval if estimated monthly GPU > $X.

maria.k: Good call. I'll add gating: if estimated monthly GPU spend > $20k open finance approval and tagging required.

chandra: Networking gotcha — ensure cross-zone NAT and sufficient ephemeral IPs for image pulls during scale-up. Also provide steps to validate MTU and TCP BBR if customers see perf drops. For internal control plane (private cluster) ensure bastion + kube-proxy reachability tests in runbook.

maria.k: Validation checklist (commands & expectations):
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide` -> nodes Ready and GPU allocable column shows GPU counts.
- `kubectl describe node <gpu-node>` -> `nvidia.com/gpu` allocatable > 0.
- Deploy tiny inference pod:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: gpu-smoke }
spec: { containers: [{ name: infer, image: ghcr.io/redwood-ai/gpu-smoke:latest, resources: { limits: { "nvidia.com/gpu": 1 } } }], restartPolicy: Never }
```
Expect the pod to schedule to GPU node and exit 0 within 30s.

maria.k: Perf smoke (simple): run a scripted inference loop hitting local model runner on cluster LB for 1 minute under `--concurrency 4` and capture p50/p95. Have a baseline in the repo.

jon.s: Add automated post-deploy checks to CI: cluster-validators job that runs the pod above + checks node-level metrics via Prometheus. Also ensure alerting: node GPU utilization < 5% for 30m -> autoscale down? and > 90% -> capacity alert.

deploy-bot: deployment/infra-tooling triggered: terraform plan for `region-us-west2` completed. No drift detected.

kevin.l: Handoff section: include owners for 2-week burn-in (who to call): infra-oncall, ml-platform, cost-control. Add a calendar invite template for 1-week review with ML and product.

maria.k: Final items I need help with:
- person to own GPU AMI bake & security hardening (who will own?).
- confirm default storage class (we prefer rwx NFS for models + fast local scratch for tensors).
- finalize tags for cost center and project.

chandra: I can owner AMI bake and driver updates for the first 30 days. I'll add steps to the runbook for patching NVIDIA drivers via SSM/guest.

maria.k: Great — I'll update runbook and push to infra repo under `runbooks/region-bootstrap.md`. Pls review PR once posted. :thumbsup:

jon.s: One last note: record exact region limitations in the runbook (e.g., no p4d in eu-west-3), maybe a table per cloud. Saves time later.

maria.k: Agreed. Will add a small matrix. Thanks all.
